headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error risks: ms-swift can read/write files and call external APIs, while the awesome-list agent is non-runnable and provides no isolation or verification boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented: agent_a is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, while agent_b uses files/stdin-stdout but no clipboard or MCP. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or file handoff, so prompt injection is possible but not default and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies agent_b output into agent_a-maintained prompts or docs
IF agent_b reads attacker-controlled text from shared files or stdin without sanitization
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Avoid copy-pasting raw model output into downstream prompts
Add a short human review step before reusing generated text
Use file naming conventions that distinguish trusted inputs from model outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b can read_filesystem and write_filesystem and touches logs, configs, datasets, and secrets like hub_token/sdk-token; agent_a has no I/O surfaces, so it is not a leak source. The pair still creates a leakage pathway if shared files contain sensitive data and agent_b uploads or echoes them through allowlisted APIs.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in agent_b's readable workspace
IF agent_b sends file contents to ModelScope, HuggingFace, vLLM, SGLang, LMDeploy, EvalScope, or OpenAI interfaces
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Restrict agent_b to a scrubbed input directory
Rotate any exposed hub_token or sdk-token
Disable outbound API calls for runs handling sensitive files
Use separate directories for logs and data

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b has write_filesystem, execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, and allowlisted network egress, while agent_a has no operational capabilities. There is no direct write-write conflict with agent_a, but agent_b can still contend with other processes over shared files or configs if the pair is co-located, so the interaction is a real default risk rather than a purely unusual one.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF another process depends on files that agent_b rewrites during execution
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Make shared files read-only during runs
Serialize file-producing steps with a simple lock file
Snapshot inputs before agent_b modifies them

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a curated list, not an executing verifier, so its outputs can be treated as authoritative references by agent_b without any built-in validation. Because agent_b can act on files, configs, and external APIs, a mistaken or stale recommendation from agent_a can cascade into incorrect operational changes or uploads.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a-curated recommendations as if they were validated instructions
IF agent_b applies those recommendations to configs, datasets, or API calls without a review step
mitigations: Require a human check before acting on curated recommendations
Tag agent_a output as reference-only
Add a verification checklist before agent_b writes files or calls APIs
Log the source of each downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: No residency or certification mismatch is documented. agent_a touches no data classes and has no I/O, while agent_b handles many data classes and secrets but the profile does not state regulated data or cross-border constraints. This is a compliance surface, but the evidence is too thin for more than low severity.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is processed through agent_b
IF retention or residency requirements apply to logs, checkpoints, or datasets
mitigations: Classify the data before running agent_b
Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Set a short log-retention policy
Document where checkpoints and logs are stored
